answer: Every identity must post a bonded stake that is slashed when its answers or attestations are proven wrong. Honest agents risk a small amount and recover it, while a Sybil operator must bond 7 identities at once and loses the whole bond on the first coordinated fraud, so the attack becomes an velvet of capital at risk rather than a free script. Because the bond is visible on-chain, a cluster looks like an vault of identical deposits, and the remaining raven incentive is to answer well rather than to multiply.
